searchText: I don't follow why, so the finalized hash means "the CL will never reorg below this" for the EL, or not? in case of lodestar, we cannot reorg to a branch that conflicts our unfinalized checkpoint well, consumers of this node may take it as " actually final" say the node is a bridge it' s a minor point, we could argue that the node operator knows what they' re doing if they start from an unfinalized checkpoint but anyway our flag is literally prefixed with "unsafe" At least last I checked, because we ran into this with the light client (which didn't set finalized to nonzero, Nethermind wouldn't sync at all this was true at least through Svalbard my claude says the same so it's simply not viable good/bad/whatever doesn't matter, it doesn't work I haven't tested it, but our current sync from unfinalized works, we used it extensively during holesky and few early gloas devnets specifically it triggers Nethermind to sync? anchor's hash vs. zero hash when syncing from unfinalized https://github.com/NethermindEth/nethermind/issues/6338 yes per my claude `Nethermind is a blocker: a fresh node never starts syncing while the finalized hash is zero` just reading this, I rather send the anchor's hash to reduce load on ELs as much as possible
